name: King of Taanach
overview: The King of Taanach was a male ruler identified as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the Israelite conquest of Canaan. His specific tribe and additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. He is noted primarily for his role as a defeated king under Joshua's campaign.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Taanach' simply denotes his rulership over the city of Taanach, as stated in Joshua 12:21. There is no further etymological or divine significance attributed to this title in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for the King of Taanach beyond his identification as a king defeated by Joshua.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Taanach's significance lies in his defeat by Joshua, which represents the fulfillment of God's promise to give the Israelites the land of Canaan. His inclusion among the thirty-one kings conquered highlights the comprehensive nature of Israel's victory under divine guidance. This defeat symbolizes the establishment of God's covenant people in the Promised Land.
